samples.question: This image shows one balance drawn on white paper: a light grey stand, a light grey beam that crosses the top of the stand, and two dark slate PANS hanging from the two ends of the beam on light grey cords. Small coloured blocks rest on the pans. THE LEFT PAN is the dark slate pan whose centre is further to the left of the page and THE RIGHT PAN is the other one. A pan HANGS LOWER than the other when the centre of its dark slate bar is nearer the bottom edge of the page, that is when it is drawn further down the page; compare only the two dark slate bars, not the blocks, the cords or the beam. The blocks are decoration for this question: the number of blocks on a pan, their colour and their size are chosen separately from the way the beam is drawn, so on some pages the pan with more blocks is the lower one and on other pages it is the higher one, and neither is a mistake. No image in this set is a borderline case: the beam is always clearly tilted, never level. Report the picture in front of you, and do not answer from how a balance would settle under the weight of the blocks. Which pan hangs lower? Answer exactly one of: left, right.
